To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the performance of XQuery is not significantly different for XML and relational data, that the performance of the relational data access is significantly better when using a relational database system that has native XML support than when using a database system that does not have native XML support, and that the performance of XML and relational data accesses are not significantly different when using a relational system that has native XQuery support.

(i) the use of XML as a data exchange format in the context of the Internet of Things has a positive effect on data exchange, (ii) the use of an XML-based data exchange format has a positive effect in terms of data quality, (iii) the use of the XML format has a positive impact on data integration, and (iv) the use of a data integration system has a positive impact in terms of data integration.

the use of a 4-layer architecture, where XML is used as the communication language between the application and the database, is a viable approach for accessing XML documents stored in a relational DBMS.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the design of a four-layered architecture for the execution of XML queries over relational databases.
the development of a software architecture for XML data processing in a database environment.
XML data management in a database environment.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the XQuery standard is not a good choice for the implementation of a database system, but that it is very useful for the implementation of an XQuery engine.
the use of XML is not only a good idea for data exchange between applications, but also for data storage and retrieval in the database.
the XQuery language is an excellent choice for querying XML data, but that it does not provide a good solution for updating XML data.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

we have designed, implemented, and experimentally evaluated a four layer architecture for processing XML data in a relational DBMS, which is based on a new SQL data type for XML and a new XQuery data type for XML fragments.
the proposed architecture is able to handle XML data in a way that is both efficient and flexible.
we have shown how to integrate XML data with relational databases and that we have provided the means for the integration of XQuery and SQL.
The main takeaway from our work is that
a 4-layer architecture, which separates data, logic, and presentation, is well suited to handle the XML data type in SQL.
the use of XML as a query result data type in a relational database system is feasible.
it is possible to use the XQuery language in a SQL-based data access architecture.
